posts.text: President Trump’s reasons for quitting NATO may miss the alliance’s rules—but the policy case remains: NATO outlived its Cold War purpose, the US pays disproportionately, and the commitments can bypass Congress. Cato’s @MWChapman argues it’s time to withdraw. ow.ly/g81L50YNu0H

Hillary Clinton recently outlined a proposal to make childcare affordable, but subsidies don't make it cheaper to provide—they mainly just shift the bill to taxpayers. Real affordability means removing  regulations that drive costs up, Cato’s @MrRBourne explains.

ow.ly/Azj150YN9KH

The Supreme Court heard a major case today on whether the FCC can impose $100M+ in penalties without a jury trial. Cato’s amicus brief argued this violates the Seventh Amendment—agencies shouldn't be judge, jury, and enforcer of their own claims. 

Read more: ow.ly/vtuF50YNEIr

Congress imposed strict limits on refrigerant production but let the EPA decide who gets to produce—handing an agency a power that belongs to Congress. SCOTUS should revive nondelegation and make Congress own the hard choices, argue Cato’s Thomas A. Berry, Brent Skorup, and Alexander Xenos. 

Learn more: ow.ly/v8LE50YNyaO

Virginia joined the National Popular Vote Compact—but the plan still has legal and practical gaps. Even after recent reforms, questions remain about recount rules, dispute resolution, and whether courts would enforce the compact. 

Learn more: ow.ly/uF5050YMU3F

Calling heavy social media use “addiction” is fueling lawsuits and new laws built on weak scientific foundation. Cato’s @dr4liberty and @AdamOmaryPhD say we’re mixing up habit, dependence, and true addiction, which could have major consequences for privacy, free speech, and innovation.

ow.ly/xtof50YMIY1

High prices are squeezing Americans – and Washington's usual fixes would only make things worse. Cato's new Handbook on Affordability offers over 100 policy ideas to lower inflation and reduce core living costs, without the empty promises.

Video

The Senate Banking Committee is holding a confirmation hearing for the next Federal Reserve Chair. Cato's @norbertjmichel breaks down what a Kevin Warsh-led Fed might look like. 

Learn more: ow.ly/IXZQ50YNrj9

Video

Pentagon officials want automakers to shift from cars to munitions. But diverting civilian production risks higher prices & inflation—while letting defense contractors off the hook for low output and high costs. Reform procurement, don’t expand the Pentagon’s reach, explains Cato’s Benjamin Giltner.

Learn more: ow.ly/qw5V50YMPCo

Can a single state’s AI rules become de facto national policy? xAI is challenging Colorado’s “algorithmic discrimination” law, arguing it regulates AI development beyond the state and raises serious First Amendment questions. This case could shape AI + speech nationwide.

ow.ly/rMAJ50YMKSz

Surviving domestic violence isn’t a crime—yet Nicole Boynton got a life sentence for defending herself and her baby. After 25 years, Georgia’s new “second look” law freed her when a judge said she “should have never been in prison.” Justice reform in action.
ow.ly/3flX50YLoZk

President Trump’s executive order may speed up psychedelic research—but it won’t fix the real problem. Strict FDA/DEA rules still block access, sideline experienced therapists, and keep treatments out of reach. Reform the system, not just the science, says Cato’s @dr4liberty.
ow.ly/ozT950YN8II

Open banking doesn’t need a mandate. Banks and fintechs are already sharing data because customers demand it (78% use fintech apps). Mandatory open banking would distort investment and lead to endless disputes. Let the market work, explain Cato’s @SolveigSinglet and Ryan Chan-Wei. 

ow.ly/BsNh50YMubs

The administration's tariffs don't just rest on bad policy — they rest on an outdated concept that no longer fits the world we live in, says economist @KyleLHandley. He explains that Section 122 was written for a monetary order that no longer exists. 
  
ow.ly/qut950YLoOC

A government-run tax filing portal can't replace the need for tax reform. As Adam N. Michel argues, it expands the IRS’s role without fixing the complexity that makes filing hard in the first place. The solution is simpler taxes—not a new website. ow.ly/n81y50YMIHn

Affordability improves as productivity rises and wages grow relative to prices. But that takes time and voters want visible, near-term price cuts.  

“The Cato Handbook on Affordability” offers a disciplined way to reduce inflation and ease living costs today, without the risks of subsidies, price controls, and regulations.

ow.ly/KoNE50YLgB7

Illegal immigrants have paid about $3 trillion in taxes over the last 30 years and likely reduced deficits by $1.7 trillion, says Cato’s @David_J_Bier. 

Check out the data: 
ow.ly/x1MF50YKHtb
